label: Postgres: Query
description: Run SQL against a Postgres database and get the rows back. The query's parameters are the node's own input ports, declared inline and read by name in the SQL: `PostgresExecuteQuery(user_id: String) { query: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $user_id" }`. A string binds as text, a boolean as bool, a number to whichever numeric column it meets, null to any column, an object or list as jsonb; cast the placeholder for other types (`$when::timestamptz`). Several statements are a script: with `$name` parameters each statement runs with the ports it names, in one transaction; without any, the script is sent whole and cells come back as text. Either way the rows of the last statement come back. Declare output ports (`-> (name: String)`) to read the first row's columns by name.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: The database's connection (wire a PostgresAccess node, or a PostgresDatabase's access output).

inputs.name: query
inputs.label: SQL
inputs.description: The SQL. Each `$name` reads the input port of that name; declare the ports inline on the node and wire them.

outputs.name: rows
outputs.description: The answered rows keyed by column name (the last statement's, for a script).
